characters.name: Underdog
characters.description: The superhero alterego of Shoeshine Boy. Blue Is Heroic: Tied withRed Is Heroic. The superhero Underdog wears a red jumpsuit with a blue cape. Catchphrase:"When (there's some kind of trouble), I am not slow./ It's hip, hip, hip, and away I go!""There's no need to fear./ Underdog is here!""Not plane, nor bird, nor even frog, it's just little old me, Underdog!" characters.name: Sweet Polly Purebred
characters.description: A TV news reporter and Underdog's love interest. Catchphrase: "Where, oh, where has my Underdog gone? Oh, where, oh, where has he gone/can he be?" Damsel in Distress: A parody of this trope. In almost every episode, she is kidnapped by villains,  delivers herCatchphrasewith a comically mournful tone, and Underdog comes to the rescue. Damsel out of Distress: Polly doesn't always just wait to be rescued, even though it's usually necessary. There is even one episode wheresheis the one who saves Underdog. Expy: To Lois Lane fromSuperman, since Underdog himself is a parody of him. Polly is a television news reporter who loves the main superhero.

characters.name: Simon Bar Sinister
characters.description: A mad scientist and recurring villain. Bar Sinister: Dr. Simon Bar Sinister is the main antagonist. Besides being ahighbrow referencetoSimon bar Kokhba, the name could be translated as "Simon, the Bastard". Benevolent Boss: Unlike a lot of villains with their henchmen, Simon treats Cad kindly and respectfully. When Cad speaks up against a flaw in Simon's plan, Simon genuinely appreciates and values Cad's constructive criticisms. Catchphrase: Simon Bar Sinister would frequently preface an imperative with "Simon says…" Depraved Dwarf: The power-hungry villain Simon Bar Sinister is shorter than most characters.

characters.name: Riff Raff
characters.description: A wolf gangster and recurring villain. Bad Boss: Riff Raff occasionally uses violent methods to punish most of his henchmen, though he usually listens to Mooch's advice more. Card-Carrying Villain: He loves being Public Enemy Number One, and once devoted an entire plan simply to recover that title. The Don: Riff Raff is a parody of the trope, being a gangster who leads a mob of cartoon criminals. Laughably Evil: While he is proud of being a gangster, his exaggerated overconfidence and his bumbling crew of criminals make him funny to watch.
